This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:

sentences.text: Prosecution story, in brief, is that at the time of the incident, the prosecutrix was aged around more than 17 years.
Prior to the incident the prosecutrix and the applicant were known to each other.
On 03.09.2023, the prosecutrix called the applicant.
Thereafter the applicant came at village of the prosecutrix and took her to village Oosalgarh by four wheeler.
The applicant took the prosecutrix along with him for six days.
Meanwhile, he committed rape upon her several times.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has not committed any offence and has falsely been implicated in the case.

It is also submitted that the prosecutrix (PW-1), her mother (PW-2) and father (PW-3) have been examined before the trial Court but they have completely turned hostile and have not supported the case of prosecution.

Parents of the prosecutrix have admitted in their deposition that the prosecutrix is aged around 19 years, therefore, it is clear that at the time of the incident the prosecutrix was a major lady and she was a consenting party for sexual intercourse, therefore, no offence is made out against the applicant.
It is also submitted that the applicant is in custody since 10.09.2023.
Trial will take considerable long time for its disposal.
On these grounds prayer is made to enlarge the applicant on bail.
5. Per contra, learned Government Advocate for the respondent/State opposed the prayer and prays for rejection of the application.
6. Learned counsel for the objector pleaded that the objector has no objection if the applicant is granted bail.
7. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and considering the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the view that applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
Hence, without commenting on the merits of the case, this application is allowed.

8. It is directed that the applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with two solvent sureties of Rs.25,000/- each out of which one shall be local surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court for securing his presence before the said Court on all the dates of hearing fixed in this regard during trial.

It is also directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) Cr.P.C.
9.

This order shall remain effective till the end of the trial, but in case of bail jump and breach of any of the pre-condition of bail, it shall become ineffective and cancelled without reference to this Bench.

10. The M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.
Certified Copy as per rules.
(PRAKASH CHANDRA GUPTA) JUDGE ns Satvir vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180598380/
